screening_decisions.reason: This is a global burden of disease estimation study using published data, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not compare early vs delayed ART initiation timing in HIV-positive people with cryptococcal meningitis.
This is a case series of 5 children with cryptococcal meningitis, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not compare early vs delayed ART initiation.
This study examines toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate-based induction therapy (antifungal treatment), not the timing of ART initiation. It does not compare early vs delayed ART.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of IRIS incidence across various opportunistic infections, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not specifically compare early vs delayed ART timing in cryptococcal meningitis.
This is a letter to the editor critiquing the Makadzange et al study, not a randomized controlled trial itself. It discusses methodological concerns but does not present original RCT data.
This is a methodological paper about the GRADE system for rating evidence quality, not a clinical study. It has no relevance to ART timing in cryptococcal meningitis.

This is a prospective observational cohort study of 65 patients, not a randomized controlled trial. All patients started ART at a median of 47 days (delayed), with no comparison group for early ART initiation.
This is an observational cohort study from Latin America, not a randomized controlled trial. While it examines ART timing (within 2 weeks vs 2-8 weeks), the comparison is not randomized.
This is a methodological paper about GRADE guidelines for systematic reviews, not a clinical study. It has no relevance to ART timing in cryptococcal meningitis.
This appears to be a letter or commentary with references to other studies, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not present original RCT data comparing ART timing.
This is a consensus case definitions paper for cryptococcal IRIS, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not compare early vs delayed ART initiation.

This is a prospective observational study of early ART in in-patients with various opportunistic infections (TB 64%, CM 10%, others). It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not specifically compare early vs delayed ART in cryptococcal meningitis patients.

This is a randomized controlled trial (COAT trial) that randomly assigned 177 HIV-infected adults with cryptococcal meningitis to early ART (1-2 weeks after diagnosis) vs deferred ART (5 weeks after diagnosis). It directly compares early vs delayed ART initiation timing in the target population and reports mortality outcomes at 26 weeks.
This is a global burden of disease estimation study, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not compare early vs delayed ART initiation.
This is a review article about antifungal drug access issues, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not compare early vs delayed ART initiation.

This appears to be a letter or commentary expressing concerns about a randomized study, not the original RCT itself. The abstract only shows an unrelated reference. It does not present original RCT data.
This is an observational study examining amphotericin B deoxycholate-related toxicities, not a randomized controlled trial comparing ART timing. It does not address early vs delayed ART initiation.

This is a descriptive longitudinal observational study, not a randomized controlled trial. It describes natural history and outcomes under local conditions without comparing early vs delayed ART initiation.

This is a randomized controlled trial (A5164) comparing early ART (within 14 days) vs deferred ART (after OI treatment completion) in patients with AIDS-related opportunistic infections. While the population includes multiple OIs (PCP 63%, CM 12%, bacterial 12%), it does include cryptococcal meningitis patients and compares early vs delayed ART timing. Given the conservative screening approach, this study is included for potential subgroup analysis of CM patients.

This is an Evidence-Based Medicine (EBM) journal commentary/review of the Bouleware et al study (the COAT trial, Study 13), not the original randomized controlled trial. The abstract describes the methods of the original study rather than presenting new primary data.

This appears to be an observational study comparing early vs deferred ART in HIV patients with cryptococcal meningitis. The abstract mentions univariate and multivariate analyses and states 'A future prospective study should be conducted to confirm this result', indicating this is not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the RCT requirement.

This appears to be a commentary or opinion piece discussing ART strategies for CNS opportunistic infections. It references other articles (Badri et al.) and discusses general treatment strategies. No indication of a randomized controlled trial design. Does not meet the RCT requirement.

This is a randomized treatment-strategy trial conducted in Botswana. HIV-infected, ART-naive adults with cryptococcal meningitis were randomized to ART initiation within 7 days (early) vs after 28 days (delayed). The study directly compares early vs delayed ART initiation in HIV-positive people with cryptococcal meningitis, meeting all selection criteria.

This is an RCT (START trial) comparing immediate vs deferred ART initiation, but the population is asymptomatic HIV-positive adults with CD4+ > 500 cells/mm³. The study does not involve patients with cryptococcal meningitis. Does not meet the population criterion (HIV-positive people with cryptococcal meningitis).

This is a prospective observational study identifying patients with symptomatic relapse of CM. It does not compare early vs delayed ART initiation in a randomized design. The study focuses on fluconazole resistance and IRIS as causes of relapse. Does not meet the RCT requirement.

This is an observational study examining IRIS in HIV patients with Cryptococcus neoformans. It does not compare early vs delayed ART initiation in a randomized design. Does not meet the RCT requirement.

This is a review article discussing cryptococcal meningitis epidemiology, diagnosis, and therapy. It is not a primary research study and does not compare early vs delayed ART initiation. Does not meet the RCT requirement.

This is a prospective observational multicenter study examining cryptococcal IRIS. It does not compare early vs delayed ART initiation in a randomized design. The abstract states 'No association between the timing of HAART initiation and the diagnosis of IRIS was identified' but this is from an observational study. Does not meet the RCT requirement.

This is a prospective, open-label, randomized clinical trial conducted in Zimbabwe. HIV-positive adults with cryptococcal meningitis were randomized to early ART (within 72 hours after CM diagnosis) vs delayed ART (after 10 weeks of fluconazole treatment). The study directly compares early vs delayed ART initiation in HIV-positive people with cryptococcal meningitis, meeting all selection criteria.

This is a review article discussing cryptococcal meningitis epidemiology, immunology, diagnosis, and therapy. It is not a primary research study and does not compare early vs delayed ART initiation. Does not meet the RCT requirement.
